## Requirements (contract)

1. Fresh reviewer first inspects code/tests/public artifacts WITHOUT reading run-ledger verdicts;
   assess all new requirements and affected older obligations.
2. Publish MET / MET-DIFFERENTLY / PARTIAL / MISSING / AT-RISK-INTEGRATION with evidence domain,
   then compare run claims and route discrepancies.
3. Coverage: each requirement id → landed evidence. Acceptance criteria: ticket ACs verified.
   Deferral truthfulness: every OPEN row owes work; nothing closed without evidence.
   Artifact integrity: digests/manifests cross-agree. Deviations: with ADRs.
4. Fresh-eyes stance: re-derive from the landed tree + artifacts, not worker summaries.
   Every gap either fixed in-ticket or filed as an owned DEFERRALS row (severity recorded).
5. Verification green: `make check`; spec/coverage/backlog/build-memory checks;
   `audit_current_state.py` discrepancy report. Ledger close-out per the authorized protocol.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every requirement and cross-stream seam has an independent verdict and owner; design docs
  alone are not MET evidence.
- [ ] No unsupported acceptance or orphan gap remains; coverage history is preserved.
- [ ] Verification green; requirement ids stamped in the PR (none owned — confirmed/stamped as
  such); anything not automatically verifiable has an owned DEFERRALS row + compensating control;
  new deviations/decisions have ADRs; run ledger/BUILD_INDEX/ledger advancement per protocol.

## Test matrix

This ticket is an audit, not new product code. Its "tests" are the deterministic verification
battery it runs: `make check` (full suite incl. Docker-gated DB tests), `check_coverage_matrix`,
`check_backlog`, `check_spec_src`, `build_backlog_md --check`, `make docs-check`,
`check-build-memory.sh`, `audit_current_state.py`, planning-tool checks
(`check_plan.py`, `render_plan.py --check`), plus artifact re-hashing over the three release
report packets. A new-behavior test is not applicable — no runtime surface changes; noted
explicitly per the contract.

## Evidence report

### Requirement verdicts

All 38 Round-10 ids received an independent verdict — see `CAPSTONE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` §(k) for the
published table: **34 MET, 2 PARTIAL (SIG-EVAL-001/002 — machinery landed, human labels deferred),
4 MISSING (SIG-EVAL-005/006/007 wholesale-deferred owners; SIG-MEM-004 pending owner P33.8)**.
Cross-stream seams: 4 MET, 1 PARTIAL (eval→human, honest deferral), 1 MISSING-by-design
(intake→production, recorded non-operational).

### Deferral truthfulness

Every OPEN row scoped to this audit owes real work and carries a machine-checkable proxy or a named
operator blocker — verified, not asserted. Eight rows previously reading OPEN are now DONE-with-
preserved-history after reconciliation (the obligation was discharged; only the leading token was
stale). No row was closed without evidence; no OPEN row was found discharged-but-unrecorded beyond
the eight stale-status rows (all repaired).

### What was not done (explicit)

- No live stage (`live_verification=false`): no hosted probes, no production verification, no
  publication, no source-rights flips, no human evaluation.
- No ADR authored: the repairs are mechanical build-memory truth corrections under the existing
  P32.7/P32.11 conventions (ADR-126 family) — no decision change. If a maintainer prefers an ADR
  for the regex/reconciliation protocol extension, one can be appended; the fix itself is
  evidence-preserving, not decision-altering.
- No DB/e2e-only re-verification beyond `make check`'s in-suite Docker runs: this ticket changed no
  DB behavior (the DEFERRALS/tooling edits are docs+build-tools); `make test-db` was therefore not
  required by the ticket's own rule — recorded explicitly per the verification clause.
- Web check not run: no `web/` file touched (recorded explicitly).
